title: Arkret Audit Release Attestation
description: Structured remote attestation for an audit applet release service under ak.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1. This is the wire form behind audit_assurance_class=attested_hardware: a verifier MUST be able to validate release-service measurement, attestation chain trust root, attestation key freshness, operator identity, Realm/Circle binding, and audit release policy digest without trusting prose declarations. The attestation binds the controlled output path for ak.audit.release; it does not add the applet to MLS and does not grant signal plaintext access. See zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §6.

realm_id.description: Realm this attestation evidence is valid for. Verifier MUST require realm_id to match the MLS Welcome / Event Envelope Realm being joined or audited; identical audit_policy_version_digest values across Realms do not make evidence portable.

audit_service_actor_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the audit release service / applet actor whose controlled output path this evidence attests. MUST match the recipient_audit_actor_id or service actor accepted by the active ak.audit.applet_binding.

service_id.description: Stable operating service did_core_id hosting the audit applet or release service. MUST match the service_id in the active ak.audit.applet_binding / ak.audit.release chain.

family.description: Attestation family. 'software_test_only' is for conformance fixtures and MUST be rejected by deployments declaring attested_hardware assurance.

measurement.description: What is actually running inside the enclave / HSM / equivalent controlled output boundary. Verifiers compare this measurement to the measurement allowed by the active audit applet binding and release policy.

code_digest.description: Hash of the audit release service binary / image / policy bundle that the enclave loads. MUST be reproducible (signed by vendor build pipeline).

policy_version.description: Release service's compiled-in policy version (e.g. semantic version or git tag). MUST appear in the Realm/Circle audit binding's allowed release-service policy versions at issued_at.

report_data.description: Optional REPORTDATA-equivalent that binds the attestation to the release service public key or output-encryption key. Lowercase hex encoding of a 32–64 byte byte-string (pattern enforces an even hex length: each byte is exactly two hex characters; total 64–128 hex characters). Receivers MUST validate this binding when present.

attestation_chain.description: Ordered attestation evidence chain: leaf attestation (signed by the enclave) → intermediate (e.g. PCK certificate, AK certificate) → root (vendor attestation root certificate). Each item is base64url-encoded DER / CBOR per platform format. Verifier MUST validate signature chain and trust the root against the Realm-declared trust root list.

attestation_key.description: The attestation public key (extracted from the leaf of attestation_chain). ak.audit.release proofs and RYW receipt validation MUST be cryptographically bound to this attested output path when audit_assurance_class=attested_hardware.

verification_method.description: DID URL the receiving verifier uses to resolve attestation_key. MUST live under audit_service_actor_id's DID Document or a DID Document explicitly delegated by the active audit binding. Fragment characters are constrained to the ASCII set `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]` (a strict subset of RFC 3986 unreserved, excluding `~`, plus `:`) for stable byte-comparable key ids; see the Arkret verification-method DID URL profile in identity/did-usage-and-verification.md section 2.2. DID method-name normalized to lowercase per W3C DID 1.0.

validity.description: Validity window of THIS evidence. Verifier MUST reject evidence outside the window. For evidence presented under audit_assurance_class=attested_hardware (ak.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1), the verifier MUST reject evidence whose window (expires_at - not_before) exceeds 90 days; Realm/service policy MAY cap it lower. Evidence with a longer window MUST be treated as an elevated-risk signal and rejected by profile policy rather than silently accepted.

revocation.description: How the verifier should check whether attestation_chain leaves / intermediates have been revoked. Required when platform supports revocation (sgx_pccs CRL, tdx PCS, etc.).

operator_principal_id.description: DID of the controlling organization actually operating this enclave / HSM. This intentionally keeps the _did suffix because it is raw external DID material being compared against service_id and Realm policy, not a protocol actor_id/principal_id alias. MUST match what the Realm policy lists as the allowed audit operator. Distinct from service_id when the operating organization is different from the technical service DID (e.g. service hosted by organization A on behalf of organization B).

audit_purpose.description: Why this audit applet release service may output audit material. MUST match the active binding/session purpose; mismatch → audit_purpose_mismatch.

audit_policy_version_digest.description: Same definition as ak.audit.ryw_receipt.audit_policy_version_digest — fixed sha256 over canonical JSON {realm_id, trust_domain, audit_binding, release_policy, release_window_policy, activation_frontier_digest, first_auditable_epoch} at the Realm policy frontier at issued_at. Lets verifier O(1) check that the policy classification this evidence was issued under matches the current binding/session state, cannot be reused across Realms, and cannot retroactively expand eligibility for already encrypted messages. This field is intentionally not hash-agile in v1; a future algorithm change requires a new schema/profile. See encoding.md §2 (canonical JSON) and audited-e2ee.md §6.

proofs.description: Detached signature(s) over the canonical evidence bytes (all fields except `proofs`), signed by operator-controlled keys distinct from the enclave attestation key. Two-key separation: the enclave attests its own measurement; the operator separately attests that this enclave is the one they intend to deploy.
